name: AS-9 scope exclusions — what the standard does not decide
definition: AS 9 deals with revenue from the sale of goods, the rendering of services, and the use by others of enterprise resources yielding interest, royalties and dividends. It does NOT deal with revenue from construction contracts, hire-purchase and lease agreements, government grants and other similar subsidies, or the revenue of insurance companies arising from insurance contracts. Separately, paragraph 3 lists items that fall outside the definition of revenue altogether.
why_it_exists: Answering with AS 9 for a transaction AS 9 excludes is a specific and silent failure mode: the answer looks sourced and is wrong, because the governing standard was never opened. This concept exists to make the boundary an explicit precondition of every other AS-9 concept, so an out-of-scope input is refused rather than answered.
inputs: the counterparty type, where it decides scope (an insurance company's insurance contracts)
whether the inflow meets the AS-9 definition of revenue at all
outputs: OUT OF SCOPE — AS 9 does not deal with it, and another standard must be consulted
NOT REVENUE — the item is outside the definition of revenue for the purpose of AS 9
preconditions: a candidate inflow has been identified
this check runs BEFORE any AS-9 recognition rule is applied
exceptions: NOT APPLICABLE — a scope boundary has no exceptions; a transaction is either dealt with by AS 9 or it is not
common_mistakes: applying AS-9 sale-of-goods criteria to a hire-purchase or lease agreement
applying AS 9 to a construction contract, which AS 9 explicitly does not deal with
treating a government grant or similar subsidy as AS-9 revenue
recording an unrealised holding gain on current assets, or an appreciation in the value of fixed assets, as revenue
recording the gross inflow in an agency relationship as revenue instead of the commission
treating trade discounts and volume rebates received as revenue, when they are a reduction of cost
legal_references: UNKNOWN — statutory backing not extracted from any downloaded source in this pass
icai_references: AS 9, paragraphs 1, 2, 3 and 4.1; and AS 9 Appendix A.9 for trade discounts and volume rebates
gst_references: NOT APPLICABLE — an AS-9 scope exclusion says nothing about whether a transaction is a supply under GST; the two boundaries are unrelated
evidence_required: the document evidencing the transaction type
for an agency relationship, evidence of the agency and of the commission amount
confidence_factors: weak when the document does not distinguish a lease or hire-purchase from an outright sale
weak when the document does not reveal whether the enterprise acts as principal or as agent
weak when a subsidy's source is not identifiable as governmental
validation_checks: the transaction is not one of the four kinds AS 9 does not deal with, before any AS-9 recognition rule is applied
the inflow is not one of the five kinds listed in paragraph 3 as outside the definition of revenue
in an agency relationship, the amount recorded as revenue is the commission, not the gross inflow
examples: goods sold and delivered by a trading enterprise — in scope, decided by ACC-REV-GOODS
an annual maintenance contract — in scope, decided by ACC-REV-SERVICES
counterexamples: a construction contract — AS 9 does not deal with it (para 2(i))
an insurance company's revenue from insurance contracts — AS 9 does not deal with it (para 2(iv))
appreciation in the value of fixed assets — outside the definition of revenue (para 3(i))
a realised gain from discharging an obligation below its carrying amount — outside the definition of revenue (para 3(iv))
